info.title: Passmint API
info.description: Issue and manage Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes. All endpoints are authenticated with a secret API key.

Event types to deliver (for example `pass.redeemed`), or `*` for all pass events (template.republished must be subscribed by name).

since.description: ISO 8601 start of the window. Required.

until.description: ISO 8601 end of the window. Defaults to now. The window is capped in length.

image_variant.description: The template image variant the pass renders with, or null for the template's own images.

status.description: The Google Wallet class sync: one write that carries the issuer name, colour, logo and hero to every Google holder. `skipped`: no pass on this template has a Google object.

objects.description: Per-pass Google object updates. Zero when the change only touched the class (name, logo, hero).

apple.description: Apple passes re-signed and pushed: those with an installed device, plus never-installed ones when the artwork changed.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable code when the error has a specific cause. Not exhaustive: treat unknown codes as the generic error for the `type`. Codes include `api_key_expired` (401, the key's expiry has passed), `insufficient_scope` (403, the key's scopes do not allow this route), `invalid_limit` (400, `limit` is negative, fractional or non-numeric; 0 is valid and a limit over the maximum is clamped), `invalid_cursor` (400, `starting_after` is not an id on this list), `republish_in_progress` (429, too many template republishes running), `republish_unavailable` (503, try again shortly) and `plan_limit_exceeded` (402).

usage.description: Live-mode usage in the current billing period (a rolling 30 days on plans without one). Pass issuance stops at api_calls.quota; other live writes continue to api_calls.grace_ceiling.

credentials.description: The organization's own signing credentials. Live passes are only signed with these, never with Passmint's shared test credentials.

warnings.description: Present only when the saved design breaks a recommended rule (an Apple field limit, a duplicate field key, an unknown barcode placeholder, an image the pass style cannot show). The template is saved; fix these before they surprise you at issuance.

image_variants.description: The template's image variant names that hold at least one image, sorted. A pass selects one with `image_variant`.

TemplateDesign.description: The template's design as stored. See CreateTemplateBody.design for the write contract.

field_values.description: The pass's field values by field key. Normally strings; any JSON value sent is stored and returned as-is.

metadata.description: Free-form key/value data you attached to the pass, or null.

post.summary: Push template changes to issued passes
post.description: Publishes the template's current design to the passes already issued from it, in this key's mode. Google Wallet gets one class update (issuer name, logo, hero) plus per-pass object updates when fields, colours or the barcode changed; Apple Wallet passes with an installed device are re-signed and pushed. Saving a template never does this on its own — call it once your edits are done. Returns 202 with the new republish, or 200 with the one already running; in that case another runs when it finishes, so the latest design reaches every pass. Archived templates can be republished too: their passes are still in wallets.

put.description: Sets this pass's own image of one slot, over its image variant's and its template's. The pass is re-rendered, re-signed and pushed to installed devices, like any update. On Google Wallet a pass strip is the object's hero image; a pass thumbnail is the object's logo on generic passes and an image module on every other type; background is Apple only. Replacing an image retires the public URL Google fetched the old one from. A voided pass is a 409 (pass_voided). If the Google Wallet object could not be updated, the request still succeeds and `warnings` says why.

schema.description: The image slot, by its Apple name: strip, thumbnail or background — whichever of those the template's style has (storeCard and coupon: strip; generic: thumbnail; eventTicket: strip, thumbnail, background; boardingPass: none).

data.description: The image, base64-encoded: PNG or JPEG (WebP is also accepted). Any resolution — it is resized to the slot's 1x and @2x sizes. 8 MB limit.

delete.description: Removes this pass's own image of one slot, so the slot falls back to the pass's image variant or its template. The stored image is deleted and its public URL stops resolving: this is also how to erase a pass image (a member photo, say), and it works on a voided pass (which is not re-rendered). Otherwise the pass is re-rendered and pushed. Deleting a slot the pass has no image of changes nothing and returns the pass.
